## RESEARCH NOTE: Banking Court procedure — FIO 2001, ss.10 and 22

### 1. Leave to defend

Section 10(1) of the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001 provides:

> The Banking Court shall not grant leave to defend the suit unless the application filed by the defendant under sub-section (2) discloses that there is a serious and bona fide dispute

Section 10(2) provides:

> The defendant shall file the application for leave to defend within thirty days of the date of first service by any one of the modes laid down in sub-section (5) of section 9

### 2. Appeals (disputed text)

Section 22(3), proviso, deals with stay of execution:

> or in the case of an appeal other than an appeal against an interim decree, at the discretion of the High Court furnishes security equal in value to such amount; and in the event of a stay being granted for a part of the decretal amount only, the requirement for a deposit in cash or furnishing of security shall stand reduced accordingly.

Section 22(6) restricts interlocutory appeals:

> No appeal, review or revision shall lie against an order accepting or rejecting an application for leave to defend, or any interlocutory order of the Banking Court which does not dispose of the entire case before the Banking Court other than an order passed under sub-section (11) of section 15 or sub-section (13) of section 15A or sub-section (7) of section 19.
